result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.group_degree_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the degree centrality of a group of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36718-L36771){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.group_degree_centrality( group, mode="all", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Group degree centrality](/assets/graphs/group-degree-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph twice. Left, the group C, F: between them they touch all five outside nodes A, B, D, E and G, drawn in accent, so the score is 5 / 5 = 1.0. Right, the group A, B reaches only C and D, 2 of 5, for 0.4." width="100%"} Group degree (Everett & Borgatti, 1999) is the share of nodes outside the group that are adjacent to at least one member: the reach of the group in a single step. Because a neighbor shared by two members counts once, members with *non-overlapping* neighborhoods give the group a wider reach than members who know the same people. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [group]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group's nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["all"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which neighbors count on a directed graph: `"all"` (default) counts both directions, `"out"` nodes the group points to (NetworkX's `group_out_degree_centrality()`, and also what its `group_degree_centrality()` computes on directed graphs), and `"in"` nodes pointing to the group (`group_in_degree_centrality()`). Ignored for undirected graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The group degree centrality, between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the group is empty, contains a node that does not exist, or `mode=` is invalid. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The two hubs of a "double star" reach every leaf between them: ::: {#ac1d03d4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["h1", "h2", "a", "b", "c", "d"]) .add_edges([("h1", "a"), ("h1", "b"), ("h2", "c"), ("h2", "d"), ("h1", "h2")]) ) graph.group_degree_centrality(["h1", "h2"]), graph.group_degree_centrality(["h1", "a"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.0, 0.5) ``` ::: :::
